candidates.title: Map recurring job alerts into a daily Slack list

demandEvidence.chore: Workflow: Schedule Trigger (daily) → Apify node (“Run an Actor and get dataset”) → IF item count > 0 → Slack.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Sharing a simple pattern I use for tracking hiring at target companies. Workflow: Schedule Trigger (daily) → Apify node (“Run an Actor and get dataset”) → IF item count > 0 → Slack. In the Apify node, run the Actor birch

experimentPlan.output: A daily digest of new job listings from a short operator supplied company and role list.
inputs: Synthetic company names and role keywords
Synthetic job listing records with title, location and URL
experimentPlan.trigger: At a scheduled daily run or when an operator supplies a sample listing batch.
steps: Read the target company and role list supplied by the operator.
Collect or accept sample listings from explicitly permitted sources.
Filter listings against the supplied targets.
Count matches and format title, location and URL.
Send a draft digest to a test Slack channel for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Given a fixed synthetic list and listing set, every matching listing appears once with its title, location and URL, and nonmatches are omitted.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies target companies, confirms permitted sources and reviews links before acting; do not scrape restricted services or represent listings as verified.
unverified: Live access and permission for each job source
Actor reliability and deduplication on real listings
Slack delivery credentials and operating cost

ease.reason: The retained post context gives a daily Schedule Trigger → Apify actor → count check → Slack flow; n8n Summarize docs support counting inputs, not scraping.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small recruiting consultancies may pay for a daily shortlist; the maker post reports no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use operator supplied sample listings and the documented daily flow; reliable site access and alert quality remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The post documents a repeatable daily listing-to-Slack loop; a person must choose target companies and verify listings, while scraper reliability is unverified.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe daily target-company hiring alerts and fields sent to Slack; this is one maker demonstration, not independent evidence of repeated buyer demand.

candidates.reason: Best scoped workflow among this batch; proposed experiment uses synthetic records until source access and buyer demand are verified.

candidates.title: Prepare resume details for repeated application forms

demandEvidence.chore: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet mapping supplied resume facts to fields in a manually supplied application form.
experimentPlan.trigger: When an operator pastes a new form’s questions and a fictional resume profile.
steps: Extract the stated fields from the form questions.
Match each field to a supplied resume fact.
Mark missing or ambiguous values for review.
Show proposed answers in a review sheet.
Have a person correct and manually submit approved answers.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed fictional profile and field list, each proposed answer matches its source fact and every unsupported or ambiguous field is left blank and flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies fictional or authorized data, checks each mapping and submits forms; never auto-submit or handle real applicant records in the prototype.
unverified: Real form layouts and field wording
No browser interaction or automatic submission is documented

ease.reason: A beginner can map supplied resume facts to operator supplied fields; Information Extractor docs support structured extraction, not browser form filling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers may pay to reduce repeated entry; the post describes one person’s task and no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic prototype can extract values into a review sheet; company forms, sensitive-data handling and live submission remain out of scope.

autonomy.reason: Structured extraction from supplied text is documented, but there is no form-filling capability; a person must verify every value and submit it.

evidence.reason: The post states a daily two-hour resume-entry chore for forms tailored to one or two companies; wider recurrence and demand are uncorroborated.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore scoped as draft-only, but the provisional mean is below six and no user demand or form-filling implementation is established.

posts.title: Turn target-company job alerts into a daily digest
posts.promise: Test a daily listing digest with synthetic data before connecting any job source.
posts.whatItIs: A small proposed service would compare a recruiter or recruiting consultancy’s chosen companies and role keywords with new listing records, then prepare a digest containing each match’s title, location and link. The supplied forum post describes a daily schedule, a job-scraping actor, a match count check and a Slack alert, and its retained context says the workflow targets hiring at chosen companies. A supplied n8n reference supports counting input records, but does not establish scraping, source permissions or Slack delivery. The four-week student version can start with synthetic records and a test destination. A person chooses target companies and permitted sources, then checks every listing before using it. This proposal does not claim that any AI service or paying customer exists.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: small recruiting consultancies that track hiring at selected companies might pay for a reviewed daily digest; no purchase or revenue evidence is supplied.
loop: An operator supplies target companies and role keywords.
A permitted source or synthetic batch provides listing records.
The workflow filters and counts matching records.
It formats title, location and link into a digest.
A person reviews listings before follow-up.
posts.evidence: The retained forum spans describe the author’s daily Schedule Trigger → Apify actor → item-count check → Slack workflow for new listings at target companies. The author says the actors remember seen jobs; this is an attributed maker claim. The n8n Summarize documentation supports counting input values, not retrieving listings.
posts.uncertainty: The excerpts do not establish permission or reliability for live job-site collection, independent demand for a paid service, or willingness to pay. The student version is a proposed test with synthetic listing rows first; live access, Slack delivery and data quality remain unverified. Human review is required.
first24Hours: Create a synthetic table of target companies, roles and listing records.
Write expected matching and nonmatching results for ten fictional listings.
Prepare a digest mock and ask one recruiting operator which fields need review.

demandEvidence.chore: Track hiring at target companies with a daily workflow that checks new job listings and sends matching details to Slack.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Sharing a simple pattern I use for tracking hiring at target companies. Workflow: Schedule Trigger (daily) → Apify node (“Run an Actor and get dataset”) → IF item count > 0 → Slack.

ease.reason: The retained post context gives a daily schedule, actor, count check and Slack flow; n8n Summarize docs support counting, but not scraping.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: recruiting consultancies may pay for a target-company digest; the maker post establishes no customer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic four-week experiment is bounded and the provided reference supports counts; permitted source access and delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The supplied workflow is a daily listings-to-alert loop; humans must select targets, verify sources and review each listing.

evidence.reason: The retained spans detail a daily alert workflow and fields; evidence is one maker’s account, without independent buyer corroboration.

steps.message: Assessed all seven sealed forum identities. Proposed one daily job-listing digest experiment based on the detailed n8n workflow; scored three concrete tasks and excluded four items without a grounded recurring chore. The other scored experiments remain below threshold.
